links.outcome: Clinical correctness and guideline adherence of CKD decision-support answers
links.effect: RAG-based methods outperformed the baseline LLM in clinical correctness and guideline adherence (no numeric values given in the abstract)
links.tradeoff: All RAG systems were limited by the scope of the indexed guideline and performed poorly when essential information was missing.
links.quote: RAG-based methods outperformed the baseline LLM in clinical correctness and guideline adherence.

links.outcome: Patient-specificity and clarity of CKD guideline-based answers
links.effect: GraphRAG achieved the highest patient-specificity, especially for threshold, algorithmic or open-ended management tasks, but scored lower in clarity (no numeric values given in the abstract)
links.tradeoff: Lower clarity, because graph walks often returned long guideline excerpts that obscured key recommendations.
links.quote: GraphRAG achieved the highest patient-specificity by leveraging multi-hop relationships across a knowledge graph derived from NICE CKD guidelines, particularly for tasks involving thresholds, algorithmic decisions, or open-ended management.

design_hint: retrieval grounding (RAG/GraphRAG) added to baseline LLM
